toegepas.rede_vinder: Afrikaans idiom is 'op dieselfde plek'; 'in dieselfde plek' follows English 'in the same place'.
toegepas.fout: 'in dieselfde plek' copies English 'in the same place'; Afrikaans says 'op dieselfde plek'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The fixed Afrikaans expression is 'op dieselfde plek', and both versions still say the springbok lives where the grass lives, so the meaning has not moved.

toegepas.voor: vol gras en baie min bome
toegepas.na: vol gras met baie min bome
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'vol ... en baie min bome' reads as 'full of very few trees'; 'met' attaches the few trees correctly without changing the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'vol gras en baie min bome' can be read as 'full of very few trees'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: With 'met', 'few trees' clearly attaches to the habitat and not to 'vol'; it is still a habitat with lots of grass and few trees.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: A river's sides are its 'walle' in natural Afrikaans; 'aan die kante' is vague and wooden.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'aan die kante' is the video's own wording and reads fine, and 'op die walle' changes the place, because reeds grow at the water's edge and not only up on the banks, which also matches the riete definition's 'langs water'.
